name: Narco-Jihad Operational Doctrine
description: Systematic use of narcotics trafficking to finance, facilitate, and destabilize target regions — specifically combining Afghan heroin production with Pakistani ISI coordination and Indian Punjab distribution networks to fund terrorist operations and degrade social fabric.

origins.historical_roots: Evolution from 1980s Afghan mujahideen drug trade through 1990s Taliban opium taxation to post-9/11 systematic ISI weaponization
origins.ideological_framing: Jihad through economic warfare — destroying enemy society through addiction while funding armed operations

downstream.destination: End-user sales fund weapons purchases, militant recruitment, operational infrastructure

financial_flow.heroin_value_multiplication: 10-20x from Afghan border to Indian retail

timeline_key_events.event: Taliban emergence — initial opium suppression then systematic taxation
9/11 aftermath — trafficking routes through Pakistan institutionalize
timeline_key_events.significance: ISI gains systematic control over logistics

timeline_key_events.event: Demonetisation (8 Nov) — financial disruption to FICN/narco networks
timeline_key_events.significance: Kinetic countermeasure; Khanani Javed dies 26 days later

intelligence_indicators: Seasonal labor migration patterns with anomalous routes
Sikh diaspora financial flows exceeding community norms
Simultaneous drug seizures and weapons cache discoveries
Khalistani rhetoric revival correlated with harvest seasons

countermeasures_documented.effectiveness: Partial — disrupted but not eliminated; doctrine adapts through alternative channels (cryptocurrency, gold, trade-based laundering)

film_relevance.dhurandhar_2_arc: Central operational threat — Rizwan Shah's mission includes penetrating this network
film_relevance.climax_connection: Demonetisation financial strike (Part 2 climax) directly targets this doctrine's financial infrastructure
